source.title: Towards Atoms of Large Language Models
source.authors: Chenhui Hu; Pengfei Cao; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE features as candidate representational units and finds them incomplete and less stable than its proposed atoms, while also testing whether threshold-activated SAEs can recover sparse units in LLMs.
record.gate_note: Included reported faithfulness and stability results for SAE feature sets, TSAE-identified units, capacity/data-scale matching, and ReLU SAE comparisons. The representation-shift results do not measure a listed claim version; cited results and hyperparameter values used only to select settings are not rows. Monosemanticity comparisons do not directly test the listed versions’ claims about polysemantic neurons or canonical SAE units.
record.test_reason: The study measures how fully public SAE features (GemmaScope, LlamaScope) reconstruct LLM activations, which bears on V5's completeness. It also trains its own threshold-activated SAEs that reach R2≈99.9% at L0≈8–9, which bears on V4's sparse recoverability. It argues SAE features fall short as the model's units, which is a restatement of V5. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that neurons (faithful but q*=0.5%) and public SAE features (R2=48.8%, q*=68.2%) are not ideal units. JumpReLU TSAEs with capacity matched to data scale find near-ideal, more monosemantic atoms in three LLMs. They also state that the baselines are used to show feature reconstruction is unreliable, not to claim their SAEs are superior.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates an AIP-based framework and threshold-activated SAEs on LLM representations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Reliable atom identification depends on TSAE capacity relative to data scale. ReLU SAE capacity increases from 4× to 7× do not improve the reported layer-10 results.

fits_no_version.finding: Public SAE features reach q*=68.2% on a coherence/sparsity uniqueness statistic; neurons reach q*=0.5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary directions satisfy compressed-sensing uniqueness conditions (low coherence relative to sparsity) for only part of the samples.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: TSAE capacity/data-scale grid search was conducted only on Gemma2-2B. Llama3.1-8B layers 30 and 31 were omitted after optimization failed. The reported feature faithfulness and stability are aggregate values; detailed per-feature numeric results are not given in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix C.5 Tables 3–5 report per-layer JumpReLU TSAE faithfulness and stability in addition to the aggregate values retained in R3–R8; these per-layer rows are omitted to stay within the row limit. Figure 4 also plots separate feature-set results without readable numerical values in the text, so the reported aggregate feature metrics are retained in R1–R2.

untested.parts: No toy networks, no sparsity-dependent phase transition, no regular geometry. AIP near-orthogonality is shown only in LLM dictionaries.
Does not test whether feature competition for capacity causes neuron polysemanticity, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Does not directly measure the spread of features across neurons. TSAE results cover only entity final-token activations in three models; the capacity sweep covers only Gemma2-2B layer 1.
Stability across seeds, widths or settings (splitting/merging) is cited, not tested. Canonicity of features is not tested empirically.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Neuron baseline: faithfulness R2=1 but stability q*=0.5%. The authors read this as implying polysemanticity.
Off-diagonal NAIP of identified atoms concentrates near zero: an overcomplete, nearly orthogonal dictionary in LLM activations.
Raw activations shown to exhibit widespread superposition, resolved by the atom decomposition (qualitative figures).
LLM-judged monosemanticity scores: GemmaScope/LlamaScope features score below TSAE atoms across models and layers.

record.verdict_notes: The TSAE results come from the authors' own method on a narrow entity-activation dataset (about 20K CounterFact entities, 4× dictionary). Near-perfect R2 there may not transfer to general-text activations, although Table 2 reports similar R2 on Wikipedia and MATH500 for an unnamed model. The V5 evidence on stability rests on a uniqueness statistic rather than cross-run stability, so only completeness (R1) is linked to V5.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments use LLMs, not small toy networks, and do not test a sparsity-dependent transition or regular toy-model geometry.
Does not test whether feature competition for capacity causes neuron polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.

Tests SAE recovery of units in three LLMs, including dependence on activation data scale and TSAE capacity. Does not test whether features are generally spread across many neurons, or establish the result across all models and data settings.

Tests faithfulness and a stability statistic for SAE features. Does not establish whether features are canonical across all decomposition settings or directly test their stability across independently trained decompositions.
Does not compare one-dimensional directions with multi-dimensional features.

conditions.value: GemmaScope and LlamaScope; listed expansion factors

rows.note: The text reports this as an average over layers and models. Authors describe the faithfulness as low and the features as short of ideal atoms.
rows.check: The value (48.8%) is right, but the baseline SAEs were trained on general text at MLP layers and evaluated on final-token activations of CounterFact entities (App. C.4). The low R2 therefore partly reflects distribution shift. R2 below 0 was clipped to 0 (Fig. 4). The state is partial for completeness: incompleteness is shown but sensitive to evaluation setting.

rows.check: q* is a coherence/sparsity uniqueness statistic (mu_q < 1/(2K_q−1)). It does not measure stability across independently trained decompositions or settings. Appendix C.5 also calls it only an upper bound for features. It is a related construct, not V5's stability, so it is moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: JumpReLU TSAEs (4×) on CounterFact entity activations, all layers of Gemma2-2B, Gemma2-9B and Llama3.1-8B; plus data-source ablation
relationships.reason: Sparse dictionaries reconstruct activations with R2≈99.9% and L0≈8–10, consistent with recoverable sparse structure (R3–R8, R10–R15).
relationships.display_finding: Sparse dictionaries reconstructed activations with R² of about 99.9% in the reported layers, consistent with recoverable sparse structure; an ablation reported L0 of about 8–10.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: JumpReLU TSAEs (4×) on CounterFact entity activations, all layers of Gemma2-2B, Gemma2-9B and Llama3.1-8B; plus data-source ablation
source_check.reason: The support label is warranted, but its coverage and numerical rationale need correction: Llama3.1-8B layers 30 and 31 are excluded, and L0≈8–10 is reported only in Table 2's ablation with unspecified model, not for each named CounterFact model. R3–R8 support near-perfect reconstruction and high structural stability in reported layers; R10–R15 support sparse reconstruction across the ablation sources.

relationships.condition: Capacity/data-scale sweep (Gemma2-2B layer 1) and ReLU SAEs on Gemma2-2B
relationships.reason: Recovery needs TSAE capacity above a threshold for the data scale (R9). ReLU SAEs reach R2 0.91–0.97 with q* 0.42–0.83, and do not improve from 4× to 7× capacity, so success depends on activation choice (R16–R41).
relationships.display_finding: Recovery required TSAE capacity above a threshold set by data scale, and ReLU SAEs reached R² of 0.91–0.97 with q* of 0.42–0.83 without improving from 4× to 7× capacity.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Capacity/data-scale sweep (Gemma2-2B layer 1) and ReLU SAEs on Gemma2-2B
source_check.reason: R9 and §4.3 show that high-fidelity recovery depends on capacity relative to data scale. Tables 3 and 6 show weaker recovery and stability with ReLU, without improvement as capacity rises from 4× to 7×. This qualifies recovery quality by method and capacity; it does not establish an absence of sparse structure.

relationships.condition: GemmaScope and LlamaScope features evaluated on CounterFact entity activations, averaged over layers and models
relationships.reason: Features explain only 48.8% of variance, so they are far from a complete account of the representation. The test is out of distribution for these SAEs (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Averaged over layers and models, the SAE features explained only 48.8% of variance, far from a complete account, though this data is out of distribution for these SAEs.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: GemmaScope and LlamaScope features evaluated on CounterFact entity activations, averaged over layers and models
source_check.reason: §4.2 reports mean R²=48.8% for public SAE features, directly showing incomplete reconstruction on these activations. Appendix C.4 identifies their continuous-text training distribution, so the result qualifies completeness in this evaluation setting rather than establishing universal failure.
